questions.q: What is the most accurate description of what @wire actually does?
options: It runs a one-time fetch exactly once when the component is created, and never again
It is a synchronous call that blocks rendering until data returns
It replaces the need for a component class entirely
It sets up an ongoing subscription to a data source, which the wire service can re-provision when the component connects, a reactive parameter changes, or the underlying cache is invalidated
questions.explain: @wire is a subscription, not a one-time fetch -- the wire service decides when to deliver (or re-deliver) data, which can happen more than once over a component's life.

questions.q: What is the difference between wiring to a property versus wiring to a function?
options: Wiring to a property is not supported in current API versions
Wiring to a function can only be used with Apex methods, never with wire adapters like getRecord

Wiring to a property exposes data/error directly on that property for the template to read; wiring to a function lets you run logic the moment new data arrives, via a destructured {data, error} parameter
There is no actual difference between the two forms
questions.explain: Property form exposes data/error directly for the template. Function form lets you intercept the data as soon as it's provisioned, to transform it or merge it with other state, by destructuring {data, error} in the method signature.

questions.q: In `@wire(getRecord, { recordId: '$recordId', fields: FIELDS })`, what does the `$` prefix on `'$recordId'` actually do?
options: It marks recordId as a reactive parameter, so the wire service re-provisions data automatically whenever this.recordId changes
It has no functional effect; it's purely a naming convention
It tells the wire service to treat recordId as a literal string value
It converts recordId into an @api property automatically
questions.explain: The $ prefix marks a wire configuration value as reactive -- a property reference the wire service watches and re-provisions data for whenever that property's value changes.

questions.q: What mistake happens if you write `{ recordId: recordId }` (no `$`) instead of `{ recordId: '$recordId' }`?
options: The component fails to compile
The wire adapter automatically adds the $ prefix for you at runtime
The wire service passes the literal string "recordId" as the parameter value instead of watching the property for changes
It behaves identically to the $-prefixed version
questions.explain: Without the $ prefix, the wire service doesn't recognize recordId as a reactive reference -- a bare property name like that would instead be interpreted as a literal string value, not re-triggering provisioning on change.

questions.q: Why can a wired property or function legitimately receive new data more than once over a component's lifetime?
options: Because @wire always re-runs on a fixed timer every few seconds
Because every wired call automatically retries three times regardless of success
Because provisioning can happen on initial connection, again when a reactive parameter changes, and again if the underlying cache is invalidated elsewhere
Multiple provisioning events never actually happen in practice
questions.explain: Because @wire is a live subscription, data can be provisioned multiple times: on connection, on a reactive parameter change, or when something invalidates the cache -- which is why handlers should correctly process data/error every time, not just on the first call.
